title: Second Largest Distinct
statement: You are given a list of integers that may contain repeated values. Find the second largest DISTINCT value in the list. If every element is equal, there is no second largest value.
input_format: Line 1: an integer n. Line 2: n space separated integers.
output_format: Print the second largest distinct value, or -1 if it does not exist.
sample_explanations: The distinct values are 9, 7, 4 and 2, so the second largest is 7.
Only one distinct value exists, so the answer is -1.
reference_solution:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
d = sorted(set(a), reverse=True)
print(d[1] if len(d) > 1 else -1)
brute_solution:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
best = max(a)
second = None
for x in a:
    if x < best and (second is None or x > second):
        second = x
print(-1 if second is None else second)

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

title: Words With Two Vowels
statement: A line of text contains words separated by single spaces. Count how many words contain at least two vowels. The vowels are a, e, i, o and u, in either upper or lower case; a repeated vowel counts each time it appears.
input_format: One line of words separated by single spaces.
output_format: Print the number of words that contain at least two vowels.
constraints: each word has 1 to 20 English letters
sample_explanations: Only 'education' has two or more vowels; 'is' and 'key' have one each.
None of the words contains a vowel.

words = input().split()
print(sum(1 for w in words if sum(c in "aeiou" for c in w.lower()) >= 2))

title: Balanced Brackets
statement: A string is made only of the characters ( ) [ ] { }. It is balanced when every opening bracket is closed by the same type of bracket and the pairs are properly nested, never crossing each other. Decide whether the given string is balanced.
output_format: Print YES if the string is balanced, otherwise print NO.
sample_explanations: Every bracket closes the most recently opened one, so the string is balanced.
The ] closes the [ while ( is still open, so the pairs cross.
brute_solution:
s = input().strip()
prev = None
while prev != s:
    prev = s
    s = s.replace("()", "").replace("[]", "").replace("{}", "")
print("YES" if s == "" else "NO")

title: Pair Sum Count
statement: Given an array of integers and a target value, count the pairs of positions i < j such that the two values at those positions add up to the target. Equal values at different positions are different pairs.
input_format: Line 1: two integers n and target. Line 2: n space separated integers.
output_format: Print the number of pairs (i, j) with i < j and a[i] + a[j] = target.
sample_explanations: The pairs are (1,5) and (3,3), so there are 2.
Every pair of the four zeros works, which is 6 pairs.
reference_solution:
n, t = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
seen = {}
count = 0
for x in a:
    count += seen.get(t - x, 0)
    seen[x] = seen.get(x, 0) + 1
print(count)

title: Maximum Subarray With One Deletion
statement: Choose a contiguous, non-empty part of the array. You may delete at most one element from the chosen part, as long as at least one element remains. Find the largest possible sum of the elements that remain.
input_format: Line 1: an integer n. Line 2: n space separated integers.
sample_explanations: Take 1 -2 0 3 and delete -2 to get 1 + 0 + 3 = 4.
Every choice is negative; the best is a single -1.
reference_solution:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
keep = a[0]
drop = float("-inf")
best = a[0]
for x in a[1:]:
    drop = max(drop + x, keep)
    keep = max(keep + x, x)
    best = max(best, keep, drop)
print(best)
brute_solution:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
best = None
for i in range(n):
    for j in range(i, n):
        part = a[i:j + 1]
        total = sum(part)
        options = [total]
        if len(part) > 1:
            options += [total - x for x in part]
        m = max(options)
        if best is None or m > best:
            best = m
print(best)

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

title: Edit Distance
statement: Given two lowercase words, find the minimum number of single-letter operations that turn the first word into the second. In one operation you may insert a letter, delete a letter, or replace a letter with another.
input_format: Line 1: the first word. Line 2: the second word.
output_format: Print the minimum number of operations.
sample_explanations: kitten to sitten, to sittin, to sitting uses three operations.
The words are equal, so no operation is needed.
reference_solution:
s = input().strip()
t = input().strip()
prev = list(range(len(t) + 1))
for i in range(1, len(s) + 1):
    cur = [i] + [0] * len(t)
    for j in range(1, len(t) + 1):
        cur[j] = min(prev[j] + 1, cur[j - 1] + 1, prev[j - 1] + (s[i - 1] != t[j - 1]))
    prev = cur
print(prev[len(t)])
